In his final earnings call before officially stepping down as Apple's CEO, artificial intelligence was the hot topic. The investment community is bullish on the potential of Siri AI to drive an iPhone upgrade cycle, while also keeping a close eye on the impact of Apple's continuously rising capital expenditures.

Cook noted that the financial outlook for Siri AI remains unclear, but he also mentioned that heavy users of Siri AI will face the iCloud+ subscription fee threshold.

Although Siri AI launched as a free feature across the iPhone, iPad, and Mac operating systems, it is in fact a service—one that Apple must continuously invest resources to operate. Depending on the nature of the request, LLM queries are sent to Apple's own cloud as well as third-party cloud infrastructure for processing.

For the first time, Apple publicly indicated that Siri AI will have a paid component. While specific usage caps have not yet been announced, Cook has hinted that users will not be able to use Siri AI for free indefinitely. Once usage accumulates to a certain level, it will be throttled, and heavy users will need to purchase an iCloud+ plan.

Without a doubt, the devil is in the details. Exactly how many free uses of Siri AI before hitting the quota limit remains unknown at this point.

Apple has previously stated that new image generation features—such as the 'Clean Up' and 'Extend' photo tools in iOS 27, as well as the redesigned Image Playground app—will come with usage limits, with iCloud+ subscribers receiving higher quotas. In the current developer and public beta versions, these restrictions are not yet in effect, so we still don't know how generous the final allowances will be.

Similarly, the new Apple Intelligence features for video recording in the Home app require a 2TB iCloud plan, while the new Cloud Pro model in the Shortcuts app is also restricted to users on higher iCloud+ tiers.

iOS 27 with Siri AI will require an iOS device or Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, and will launch later this year. For iPhones, that means iPhone 15 Pro or later models. Due to regulatory restrictions, Siri AI will not be available in Europe and China in the foreseeable future.
